abstract_sentences.text: Public research results on large-scale supervised finetuning of AI agents remain relatively rare, since the collection of agent training data presents unique challenges.

evidence.anchor: Public research results ... remain relatively rare

abstract_sentences.text: In this work, we argue that the bottleneck is not a lack of underlying data sources, but that a large variety of data is fragmented across heterogeneous formats, tools, and interfaces.

evidence.anchor: data is fragmented across heterogeneous formats, tools, and interfaces

abstract_sentences.text: To this end, we introduce the Agent Data Protocol (ADP), a light-weight representation language that serves as an “interlingua” between agent datasets in diverse formats and unified agent training pipelines downstream.

The design of ADP is expressive enough to capture a large variety of tasks, including API/tool use, browsing, coding, software engineering, and general agentic workflows, while remaining simple to parse and train on without engineering at a per-dataset level.

evidence.anchor: expressive enough to capture a large variety of tasks

abstract_sentences.text: In experiments, we unified a broad collection of 13 existing agent training datasets into ADP format, and converted the standardized ADP data into training-ready formats for multiple agent frameworks.

evidence.anchor: 13 existing agent training datasets into ADP format

abstract_sentences.text: We performed supervised finetuning on the unified data, and demonstrated an average performance gain of ∼20% over corresponding base models, and delivers state-of-the-art or near-SOTA performance on standard coding, browsing, tool use, and research benchmarks, without domain-specific tuning.

claim_closure.claim: ADP unifies heterogeneous agent data with a simple expressive schema.
claim_closure.method_response: Pydantic Trajectory with three Action and two Observation types plus automated validation.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Converters cover 13 datasets and three harnesses; Appendix B gives one field-level example, but no fidelity or error-rate audit.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion repeats lightweight interlingua and scalable pipeline.

claim_closure.claim: ADP Dataset V1 is a 1.3M-trajectory, largest publicly available agent-training dataset.
claim_closure.method_response: Table 1 inventories 13 sources; Appendix C defines the sampled mixtures.
claim_closure.evidence_response: The 1.3M raw size is explicit, but no systematic census supports the superlative; effective training sets are about 30K/20K.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recovers scalability without restating the size or superlative.

evidence.anchor: largest publicly available dataset for agent training

claim_closure.claim: ADP training yields about 20% average improvement and SOTA or near-SOTA performance.
claim_closure.method_response: Same SFT pipeline and three harnesses evaluate several model sizes.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 3–5 show direct base pairs and prior-work rows, but the average formula and uncertainty are absent and SOTA conditions are heterogeneous.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not recover the quantitative result.

evidence.anchor: Other rows are collected from previous works

claim_closure.claim: Diverse ADP data improves over task-specific tuning and avoids negative transfer.
claim_closure.method_response: Per-dataset sampling forms mixtures; matched comparisons hold harness+model fixed.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 6 favors ADP in five comparisons and Table 10 controls sample count; Base rows needed to identify below-base negative transfer are absent.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion only broadly mentions scalable training.

claim_closure.claim: ADP training is cross-domain and requires no domain-specific tuning.
claim_closure.method_response: The schema is cross-domain, but each harness receives a domain-filtered subset.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix C.1 excludes web data for OpenHands/SWE-Agent and excludes coding/SWE data for AgentLab.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion repeats scalable training without this scope boundary.

claim_closure.method_response: Common Action/Observation fields supply comparable trajectory statistics.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 compares rounds, action shares, and thought coverage for all 13 datasets.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion explicitly recovers systematic analysis across sources.

claim_closure.claim: ADP changes converter effort from O(D×A) to O(D+A).
claim_closure.method_response: Each dataset has one Raw→ADP converter and each harness one ADP→SFT converter.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Topology supports the asymptotic count; actual effort uses LOC proxy and three-harness average extrapolated to A=100.

claim_closure.claim: Open-source code and data make the work reproducible.
claim_closure.method_response: Reproducibility Statement points to schema, converters, datasets, pipeline, benchmarks, code, and data.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix adds sampling, examples, and licenses; training hyperparameters, seed value, hardware, and selection protocol remain missing.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls for continued open-source releases.

evidence.anchor: release all code and data open source

claim_closure.claim: ADP preserves critical information across diverse tasks.
claim_closure.method_response: Expressive typed Action/Observation schema and framework converters are described.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Successful benchmark training and one conversion example are indirect evidence; no reconstruction, field-loss, or conversion-error metric is reported.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion repeats a unified schema but not preservation fidelity.

evidence.anchor: preserving critical information across diverse tasks
maintaining data provenance and semantic structure
used LLMs to aid and polish writing

final_judgment.single_storyline: [p.2 §1; p.5–6 §3.3–3.4/Figure 2] Agent-data usability is framed as a representation-fragmentation problem; ADP decomposes many-to-many Raw→harness conversion into Raw→ADP and ADP→SFT, then reuses the schema for training and analysis.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: [p.3–10, Tables 1–8] The main text retains schema components, converter topology, sources, harnesses, benchmarks, descriptive dataset statistics, accuracy comparisons, mixture comparison, and LOC accounting.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: [p.16–21, Appendices B–F] Field-level examples, sampling weights, seed/shuffle statement, domain filtering, scaling plots, equal-scale control, and licenses move to the appendix; Appendix C.1 materially changes the scope of cross-domain training.
final_judgment.best_pattern: [p.6 Figure 2; p.10 Tables 7–8] A topology figure first explains many-to-many versus hub-and-spoke structure, then LOC tables quantify implementation scale while keeping structural and empirical claims separable.
final_judgment.largest_gap: [p.1 Abstract; p.9 Table 6; p.19 Appendix C.1] Harness-specific domain filtering conflicts with the literal no-domain-specific-tuning claim; the ∼20% aggregate lacks a formula/uncertainty; the negative-transfer discussion names Base but Table 6 omits Base rows.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: [p.7 §5.1; p.9 Table 6; p.19 Appendix C.1] When representation unification, data mixing, and efficacy form one argument, the main setup must show each harness’s consumed domains, effective sample count, exclusions, and every control condition invoked by the result prose.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: [p.4–5 §3; p.18–19 Appendix C] This rule applies when mixtures change method meaning or causal interpretation. A pure interoperability paper may move sampling detail to an appendix, but should still separate schema coverage, conversion fidelity, and downstream efficacy.

evidence_coverage.counting_rule: One record per claim-bearing array entry; final-judgment evidence is embedded in each string and page-map sections use start/end pages, so neither is double-counted.
